search_log.scope: BORI CE Droṇaparvan 7.45.8–7.48.13, Abhimanyu’s entry into the vyūha through his death
search_log.method: Checked the Sanskrit critical text for named individuals and verse-level combat actions; only individually named fighters were represented. Existing canonical figures are reused through known expansion IDs; anonymous units, anonymous charioteers, and unnamed sons were not made into nodes.

notes: This passage is already familiar from war narratives, so the batch prioritizes additional named fighters: Lakṣmaṇa, Kratha, Vṛndāraka, Kosala’s Bṛhadbala, Aśvaketu, the Mārtikāvata Bhoja, and five named warriors killed at 7.47.15, plus named archers in the 7.47.25 roster.

Lakṣmaṇa is the son of Duryodhana in 7.45.8–17 and is kept separate from the unrelated Lakṣmaṇa in the prior Yama roster. The Kosala king Bṛhadbala is kept separate from similarly named Gāndhāra/Kaurava attendees in the Ādiparvan batch.
The names Suvarcas, Pratardana, and Vṛṣasena occur in other rosters; they are retained as source-local fighters here because the text does not establish identity with those earlier roster entries.

The text says Aśvaketu is a son of the king of Magadha but does not name the father; no unnamed person node is created. The Kratha warrior’s son in 7.45.21–25 and Duḥśāsana’s son in 7.48.9–13 are not individually named and are omitted.

Two Vṛndāraka records are kept separate: one is killed at 7.46.12, while a Vṛndāraka appears in the attack roster at 7.47.25. Because the same passage does not establish that these are the same individual, the batch preserves the namesake ambiguity rather than harmonizing or merging them.
The six unnamed ministers killed in 7.47.5 and the group labels in 7.48.7–8 are omitted.
